binders: This is a closed proposition about mu=expMeasure(1) on R and X(x)=2x-2.
Inside the final negation, C ranges over real cutoffs and t universally over real thresholds.
conclusions: The fixed measure is a probability measure.
The integral of X is zero.
The exponential-moment gauge of X is finite.
The Unit-indexed singleton family containing X is independent.
There is no C>0 such that for every t>=max(0,C), P{X>=t}<=2 exp(-t).
mathematical_definitions: mu is the rate-one exponential measure.
The gauge is the ENNReal infimum of finite nonzero scales whose exponential absolute moment is at most two.
The final negated existential says the coefficient-one exponential upper-tail profile fails after every positive cutoff.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The centered scale-two rate-one exponential random variable is measurable, integrable, mean zero, has finite exponential-moment gauge, and forms an independent singleton family, but its upper tail cannot eventually be bounded by 2e^{-t} after any positive cutoff.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is closed and distribution-specific.
The independence assertion is for a singleton family.
The obstruction concerns the one-sided upper tail, not an absolute-value event.
It rules out only the profile 2e^{-t}, not exponential tails with a different positive rate.
The cutoff must be positive and the tested thresholds satisfy t>=C and t>=0.
Gauge finiteness supplies no explicit numerical gauge value.
Because this is a conjunction, none of its assertions is discharged vacuously by a false premise.
ambiguities: The packet exposes expMeasure only through gammaMeasure(1,1), not its density.
The gauge is described structurally rather than assigned a standard source name.
The final negated existential is classically equivalent to arbitrarily late violations of the bound.
